name: Makalu Base Camp
tagline: From rice terraces near 500 m to Makalu's south face at 4,870 m
meta_description: Makalu Base Camp, about 4,870 m in Makalu Barun National Park: trek from Tumlingtar via Shipton La and the Barun valley. Permits, season, route.
summary: Makalu Base Camp, at about 4,870 m at the head of the Barun valley, sits below the south face of Makalu (8,485 m), the world's fifth highest mountain. The trek starts near Tumlingtar in the Arun valley and crosses the Shipton La into Makalu Barun National Park. It takes about two to three weeks and stays wild.
intro: Few treks in Nepal cover as much ground in height and climate as the walk to Makalu Base Camp. It begins in the hot, low Arun valley near Tumlingtar, among rice fields, sal forest and Rai villages, and ends on moraine at the foot of Makalu's south face, under snow and ice. In between are some of the least disturbed forests in the Himalaya.

The route climbs from Num and Seduwa to Tashigaon, the last permanent village, then over the Shipton La, a high ridge with two passes and a string of small lakes, before dropping into the Barun valley. From there it follows the Barun river up through yak pastures at Yangle Kharka and Langmale to the base camp. Each stage brings a new world: rice and bamboo, then oak and rhododendron, then fir, then grass, rock and ice.

Teahouses are basic and few, and the trail sees a small fraction of Everest's traffic. It suits trekkers who have done a high trek before and want quiet, forests and a big mountain at the end, rather than comfort. Expect long days, steep climbs and descents, cold nights and simple food. In return you get some of the wildest country in Nepal, and a base camp that still feels remote.

story.title: The park that climbs eight kilometres
paras: Makalu first drew climbers in 1954, when an American team from California and a New Zealand party that included Edmund Hillary explored its approaches. The following year a French expedition led by Jean Franco succeeded: on 15 May 1955 Lionel Terray and Jean Couzy reached the summit, and over the next days the rest of the team, including Gyalzen Norbu Sherpa, followed. It was one of the first expeditions to put almost its whole climbing team on top of an eight-thousander.

In 1992 Nepal declared Makalu Barun National Park as an eastern extension of Sagarmatha National Park, covering about 1,500 km² with a buffer zone to the south and south-east. The Barun valley at its core was set aside as a strictly protected area, with its forests and alpine meadows left largely untouched. The buffer zone around the park includes the villages of the approach, such as Seduwa and Tashigaon, where people continue to farm, graze animals and collect forest products under local rules.

The park runs from the Arun valley at a few hundred metres to Makalu's summit, a rise of more than 8,000 m. Few protected areas on earth hold tropical forest and snow peaks of this height together. For trekkers, that means walking through almost every climate zone of the Himalaya in two weeks, from warm valleys where bananas grow to glaciers at nearly 5,000 m. The park shares its northern border with the Qomolangma reserve in Tibet.

legend: Sherpa and Rai stories speak of Khembalung, a beyul or hidden sacred valley in the Makalu-Barun country, said to have been set aside by Guru Rinpoche as a refuge for the faithful in times of trouble. Caves in the lower park are linked to the legend and visited by pilgrims. Locals say only those with the right merit can find the hidden valley's true heart.
people: The lower villages on the approach, such as Num and Seduwa, are home mainly to Rai families, with Sherpa, Gurung, Chhetri and other households. Tashigaon, the last permanent village, has Sherpa and Rai families. They farm millet, maize, potatoes and cardamom, keep cattle and yaks, and work as porters, guides and lodge-keepers. Higher up, herders use the kharka only in summer.

untold.fact: Makalu Barun National Park was established in 1992 as the eastern extension of Sagarmatha National Park, covering about 1,500 km² with a buffer zone of about 830 km² to the south and south-east.
From the Arun river valley at about 344 m to the summit of Makalu, the park spans an elevation gain of about 8,000 m, enclosing both near-tropical forest and snow peaks.
Makalu was first climbed on 15 May 1955 by Lionel Terray and Jean Couzy of a French expedition led by Jean Franco, with the rest of the team summiting over the following days.

taste.name: Kodo ko dhido
taste.text: A thick, smooth paste of finger-millet flour stirred into boiling water, eaten with dal, greens and pickle. It is the everyday food of the hill villages along the lower Makalu trail. Lodges in Seduwa and Tashigaon can make it on request, given some notice.

Makalu south face, Barun valley, Makalu Barun National Park

highlights.title: Makalu's south face
highlights.text: At base camp the south face of Makalu, the world's fifth highest mountain, rises steeply above the moraine. Its four-sided pyramid shape is one of the most striking in the Himalaya, best seen in clear morning light.

highlights.title: Crossing the Shipton La
highlights.text: The trail crosses a high ridge at around 4,100–4,200 m, with two passes, Keke La and Shipton La, and small lakes between. Snow can close it in winter and spring; it is the hardest day of the approach.

highlights.title: The Barun valley
highlights.text: A deep glacial valley with sheer walls, waterfalls and yak pastures, the protected core of the park. Above Yangle Kharka the views open to Chamlang, Baruntse and finally Makalu, rising at the head of the valley.

highlights.title: Forests of the lower park
highlights.text: Between Tashigaon and Khongma Danda the trail passes through rhododendron, oak, fir and bamboo forest, home to red pandas, Himalayan black bears and many birds. In April the rhododendrons bloom red and pink along the climb.

highlights.title: Rai villages of the Arun
highlights.text: The trek begins among Rai farming villages in the warm Arun valley, with millet terraces, cardamom and bamboo. Num and Seduwa face each other across the Arun gorge, with a long descent and climb between them.

how_to_reach.text: Fly from Kathmandu to Tumlingtar (about 45 minutes, schedules vary by season), then drive by jeep via Khandbari toward Num, a long day on rough road. Flights are often delayed by weather; check current status before you travel.

Tumlingtar and Khandbari can be reached by road from the Terai via Dharan, Dhankuta and Hile in about 10–14 hours, or in two days from Kathmandu. Jeeps continue toward Num and Seduwa as far as the road is passable.
From the road head, the walk to Makalu Base Camp takes about 8–10 days up via Seduwa, Tashigaon, Khongma Danda, the Shipton La, Yangle Kharka and Langmale, and 5–6 days back.

where_to_stay: Teahouses on the Makalu trail are simple family lodges, with twin or dormitory rooms, shared toilets, a stove in the dining room and limited menus. Seduwa and Tashigaon have the most choice. Above Tashigaon, lodges at Khongma Danda, Dobate, Yangle Kharka, Langmale and base camp are basic and may close outside peak season. Many groups still camp. Bring a sleeping bag rated to about minus 15 °C.
tips: Do not attempt the Shipton La in heavy snow; we build a spare day into every Makalu itinerary for weather.
Bring enough cash in Nepali rupees for the whole trek; there are no ATMs beyond Khandbari.
Acclimatise at Khongma Danda and again in the upper Barun before going to base camp.
Carry leech socks or salt for the lower forests in April, May and September.
Make sure your insurance covers helicopter rescue to at least 5,000 m.

experiences.title: Crossing the Shipton La into the Barun
experiences.summary: The hardest and most beautiful day on the approach: from Khongma Danda over the Keke La and Shipton La ridge, past small lakes and prayer flags, then down into the forested upper Barun valley.
body: We leave Khongma Danda early, often before 6 am, with a packed lunch and plenty of water. The trail climbs steeply over rocky ground to the first pass, then traverses past a string of small lakes to the Shipton La, with prayer flags marking the high points. The ridge is around 4,100–4,200 m, and on clear mornings the views open toward Makalu and Chamlang, with the forested valleys you have climbed through far below.

The Shipton La is named after the British explorer Eric Shipton. After the second pass the trail drops steeply through rhododendron and fir toward Dobate or Yangle Kharka in the Barun valley, losing well over a thousand metres in places. It is a long day, 7–9 hours, and tiring on the knees, so walking poles are a big help. Our guide keeps the group together on the ridge, where cloud can roll in fast and the trail is easy to lose.

Snow can make the crossing dangerous, especially in winter and early spring, when the traverse between the passes can be icy and the trail buried. Our guide checks conditions with lodge-keepers and other groups coming the other way, and will wait a day if needed. That is why every Makalu itinerary we plan has a spare day. Reaching the Barun valley that evening, tired but safe, is one of the great moments of the trek.

faqs.q: How high is the Shipton La?
faqs.a: The Shipton La crossing is usually given as around 4,100–4,200 m, with the Keke La nearby at a similar height. Figures vary between maps. It is the highest point of the approach before the Barun valley.

faqs.q: Is the Shipton La dangerous?
faqs.a: In good conditions it is a hard but non-technical trekking day. Snow and ice, which are common from December to April, make it slippery and route-finding difficult, and accidents have happened. Cross only with a guide who knows current conditions.

faqs.q: Why is it called the Shipton La?
faqs.a: The pass is named after Eric Shipton, the British mountaineer and explorer who led Himalayan reconnaissance expeditions in the 1930s to 1950s. Local people also have their own names for the passes and lakes on the ridge.

experiences.title: Morning at Makalu Base Camp
experiences.summary: A morning at about 4,870 m beneath Makalu's south face, with time to walk the moraine for views of the Barun Glacier, Makalu and the peaks around the head of the valley before cloud builds.
body: Base camp is a stony shelf beside the Barun Glacier, used by climbing expeditions in season, with old tent platforms, cairns and prayer flags. In the early morning, Makalu's south face catches the first light above you, its rock and ice standing more than 3,500 m higher. It is a steep, forbidding wall, and you understand at once why the first ascent came from a different side of the mountain.

We walk up the moraine slopes nearby for a wider view, as far as altitude and weather allow, usually for an hour or two. Our guide names the peaks and the glacier features, and tells the story of the 1955 French first ascent and the later climbs of the south face. The air is thin and cold, so we move slowly, eat and drink often, and turn back at the first sign of trouble.

By late morning cloud usually rises from the valley, so the best views come early. We head down toward Langmale or Yangle Kharka in the afternoon, losing height for a better night's sleep and a warmer evening. Over the next days, the walk out retraces the Barun valley and the Shipton La, and the forests and villages feel very different on the way down, with base camp behind you.

faqs.q: How high is Makalu Base Camp?
faqs.a: Makalu Base Camp is usually given as about 4,870 m, at the head of the Barun valley. Makalu itself is 8,485 m in most references, though recent surveys give slightly different figures. Either way, base camp is high enough for altitude sickness to be a real risk.

faqs.q: Can you see Everest from Makalu Base Camp?
faqs.a: The main view from base camp is Makalu's south face and the peaks around the Barun Glacier. Some trekkers climb higher on the moraine slopes for wider views on clear days. Ask your guide on the day; we only go higher if everyone is well acclimatised.

faqs.q: Are there lodges at Makalu Base Camp?
faqs.a: Basic seasonal lodges have operated at or near base camp in recent seasons, but they may be closed outside October–November and April–May. Many groups camp with their own crew and tents. We confirm what is open before each trek and plan around it.

experiences.title: Forest wildlife walk in the lower park
experiences.summary: A slow early walk through the rhododendron, oak and bamboo forests between Tashigaon and Khongma Danda, with a guide who knows the birds and signs of red panda, black bear and musk deer that live here.
body: Makalu Barun National Park protects some of the richest forests in the Himalaya. The park records 88 species of mammals, including red panda, clouded leopard, snow leopard and Himalayan black bear, and many birds. Between Tashigaon and Khongma Danda the trail climbs through layers of forest: oak and chestnut low down, then rhododendron, magnolia and bamboo, then fir and birch, all hung with moss in the damp air.

We set out early from Tashigaon or a forest camp and walk quietly, stopping to listen and scan. You are most likely to see birds: pheasants, laughingthrushes, sunbirds and minivets, and with luck a Himalayan monal flashing blue and green across a clearing. Our guide shows you the signs of larger animals, such as feeding marks on bamboo or claw marks on trees, and explains how the forest changes with altitude.

Sightings of red pandas or bears are rare and need luck, and we never chase or bait animals. The forest itself, mossy and green, is reason enough for the walk. In April and May it is full of birdsong and rhododendron blossom; in October and November it is quieter, with clearer air and golden light through the trees. Bring binoculars, and be ready to stand still for a long time.

faqs.q: What wildlife lives in Makalu Barun National Park?
faqs.a: The park records 88 mammal species, among them snow leopard, clouded leopard, red panda, Himalayan black bear, musk deer and grey langur, along with hundreds of bird species. Most animals are shy, and trekkers usually see birds, langurs and signs rather than big mammals.

faqs.q: When is the best time for birdwatching on the Makalu trek?
faqs.a: April and May, when birds are breeding and singing, and the rhododendrons are in bloom in the forests below Khongma Danda. October and November are also good, with clearer skies and easier walking but quieter forests.

faqs.q: Is it safe to walk in the forest with bears?
faqs.a: Himalayan black bears are rarely seen and usually avoid people. Walk in a group, talk at normal volume and never approach an animal or leave food around camp. Your guide knows how to respond calmly if you meet one on the trail.

experiences.title: An evening in Tashigaon, the last village
experiences.summary: A night in Tashigaon, the last permanent village on the Makalu trail, with time to walk the fields, meet porters and herders, and hear how families here live between the forest, their farms and the trekking season.
body: Tashigaon sits at about 2,100 m on a ridge above the Arun's side valleys, the last settlement before the forest and the high passes. It has a few lodges, a small shop, fields of millet and potatoes, and a view down the valley toward Seduwa and Num. Houses are scattered across the slope, with cattle sheds, maize stores and small shrines, and in the evening smoke rises from every kitchen roof.

We arrive in the afternoon and walk the village with our guide. Families here are Sherpa and Rai, and many young men work as porters for the season, while others work abroad. Conversation often turns to the changes the road and trekkers have brought, and to the long walk to school and market. You may be invited into a kitchen for tea, and see how millet is ground and dhido is cooked.

It is also the place to restock and rest before the steep climb to Khongma Danda, which gains about 1,400 m in a day. Buy any last snacks here; there is little for sale above. We repack loads with the porters, check everyone's gear for the cold days ahead, and have an early night. The next morning the forest begins just above the village, and the real climb starts.

faqs.q: What is the altitude of Tashigaon?
faqs.a: Tashigaon is at about 2,100 m. From here the trail climbs steeply to Khongma Danda at around 3,500 m, which is why many itineraries spend a night at Khongma Danda to acclimatise before crossing the Shipton La.

faqs.q: Can I hire a porter in Tashigaon?
faqs.a: Porters from Tashigaon and nearby villages work the Makalu trail, but we arrange porters in advance so they are properly insured and equipped with warm clothing and shoes for the high passes. Hiring on the spot in peak season can be difficult.

faqs.q: Are there shops in Tashigaon?
faqs.a: There are small shops selling snacks, biscuits, noodles and basic supplies at higher prices than the lowlands, because everything is carried in. Above Tashigaon there is very little for sale, so stock up here on anything you need for the next week.

faqs.q: How long is the Makalu Base Camp trek?
faqs.a: Most itineraries take 16–20 days from Kathmandu and back, including the flight to Tumlingtar, jeep to the road head, about 8–10 days walking up and 5–6 days down, plus spare days for weather. Roads in the lower valley are changing the start points. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How hard is the Makalu Base Camp trek?
faqs.a: It is strenuous. Days are long, with big climbs and descents, a high pass crossing at Shipton La, simple lodges and few rescue options. It is best for trekkers who have already done a high-altitude trek such as Everest or Annapurna base camp.

faqs.q: What permits do I need for Makalu Base Camp?
faqs.a: You need a Makalu Barun National Park entry permit, and possibly local municipal fees. Since April 2023 foreign trekkers in national parks must trek with a licensed guide. Fees and rules change; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is the best time to trek to Makalu Base Camp?
faqs.a: October to November for clear skies and stable weather, and late April to May for warmer days and rhododendrons lower down. The Shipton La is often snowbound from December to March. June to September brings monsoon rain, leeches and cloud.

faqs.q: Where does the Makalu trek start?
faqs.a: Most treks start by flying from Kathmandu to Tumlingtar, then driving by jeep via Khandbari toward Num or Seduwa. From there the walk climbs to Tashigaon, the last village, and over the Shipton La into the Barun valley.

faqs.q: Are there teahouses on the Makalu trek?
faqs.a: Yes, but they are basic and fewer than on popular treks. Seduwa and Tashigaon have the most choice. Above, lodges at Khongma Danda, Yangle Kharka, Langmale and base camp are simple and may close outside peak season. Many groups camp.

faqs.q: How high is Makalu?
faqs.a: Makalu is 8,485 m in most references, the fifth highest mountain in the world, on the Nepal–China border about 19 km south-east of Everest. Its four-sided pyramid shape makes it easy to recognise from far away.

faqs.q: Is altitude sickness a risk on the Makalu trek?
faqs.a: Yes. The trail gains height quickly from Tashigaon to Khongma Danda and over the Shipton La, and base camp is at about 4,870 m. Follow an itinerary with acclimatisation nights, drink water and descend if symptoms get worse.

faqs.q: Can I combine the Makalu trek with Everest?
faqs.a: Strong, experienced trekkers sometimes link the Makalu area with the Everest region over high glaciated passes, but that is a mountaineering route needing technical gear and an expedition crew. Most trekkers return to Tumlingtar and fly to Kathmandu.
